statement: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs was Disney's first full-length animated movie.
why: It came out in 1937. Critics called it "Disney's Folly" before it became a massive hit.

statement: Walt Disney himself was the original voice of Mickey Mouse.
why: Walt voiced Mickey from 1928 until 1947.

statement: Steamboat Willie was the first Mickey cartoon with synchronized sound.
why: Mickey had already starred in two silent shorts, but Steamboat Willie's sound in 1928 made him a star.

statement: Walt Disney almost named Mickey Mouse "Mortimer".
why: His wife Lillian thought Mortimer sounded too stuffy and suggested Mickey instead.

statement: Mickey and Minnie Mouse share the same official birthday.
why: Both debuted in Steamboat Willie on 18 November 1928, so Disney celebrates them on the same day.

statement: Donald Duck's middle name is Fauntleroy.
why: His full name, Donald Fauntleroy Duck, appears on his draft card in the 1942 short Donald Gets Drafted.

statement: Goofy and Pluto are both dogs.
why: One walks and talks, the other doesn't, but Disney confirms they're both dogs.

statement: Toy Story was the first feature film made entirely with computer animation.
why: Pixar's Toy Story came out in 1995 as the first fully computer-animated feature.

statement: Walt Disney died before Walt Disney World opened.
why: Walt died in December 1966. The Florida resort opened in October 1971.

statement: Cinderella Castle in Florida is taller than Sleeping Beauty Castle in California.
why: Cinderella Castle is about 189 feet tall. Sleeping Beauty Castle is only about 77 feet.

statement: Disneyland in California opened in 1955.
why: It opened on 17 July 1955 in Anaheim.

statement: Elsa was the villain in early drafts of Frozen.
why: The writers changed her into a hero after hearing the song Let It Go.

statement: We Don't Talk About Bruno reached a higher chart spot than Let It Go.
why: Bruno hit No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 2022. Let It Go peaked at No. 5.

statement: Ariel has six older sisters.
why: Aquata, Andrina, Arista, Attina, Adella and Alana. Ariel is the youngest.

statement: Flounder from The Little Mermaid isn't actually a flounder.
why: Despite his name, Disney says he's a tropical fish.

statement: Rapunzel's weapon of choice in Tangled is a frying pan.
why: She knocks out Flynn Rider with it, and it keeps coming in handy.

statement: Rapunzel's chameleon sidekick is named Pascal.
why: Pascal is her best friend in the tower.

statement: Stitch's original name is Experiment 626.
why: Dr. Jumba Jookiba created him as Experiment 626 before Lilo named him Stitch.

statement: Dopey is the only one of the Seven Dwarfs who never speaks.
why: As Happy explains, Dopey doesn't know if he can talk because he's never tried.

statement: Scar's three hyena sidekicks are Shenzi, Banzai and Ed.
why: Shenzi is the leader, Banzai is the hothead, and Ed only laughs.

statement: Ursula the sea witch is part octopus.
why: Her lower half has octopus tentacles. Six of them on screen, to be exact.

statement: Tiana from The Princess and the Frog dreams of opening her own restaurant.
why: It was a dream she shared with her late father, and it comes true at the end.

statement: Moana's pet pig is named Pua.
why: Pua is the pig. Heihei is the chicken who ends up on the boat.

statement: Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson voices Maui in Moana.
why: He also sings Maui's song, You're Welcome.

statement: Robin Williams voiced the Genie in the original Aladdin.
why: He improvised so much in 1992 that hours of extra recordings were left over.

statement: Dory from Finding Nemo has short-term memory loss.
why: She says so herself, and her sequel Finding Dory is built around it.

statement: In Encanto, Mirabel is the only Madrigal grandchild without a magical gift.
why: Her sisters and cousins all get gifts. Even little Antonio gets his early in the film.

statement: Dumbo's "magic" feather wasn't actually magic.
why: The crows gave it to him to build his confidence. He could fly with his ears all along.

statement: Lumière in Beauty and the Beast is a candelabra.
why: He's the castle's charming candelabra who leads the song Be Our Guest.

statement: Pixar's Coco is set during Día de los Muertos.
why: Miguel crosses into the Land of the Dead during Mexico's Day of the Dead holiday.

statement: Walt Disney's body was cryogenically frozen.
why: A famous myth. Walt was cremated in 1966 and his ashes rest at Forest Lawn in Glendale, California.

statement: Mickey Mouse was the first cartoon star Walt Disney created.
why: Oswald the Lucky Rabbit came first in 1927. Walt lost the rights to Universal, then created Mickey.

statement: Walt Disney animated Steamboat Willie all by himself.
why: His partner Ub Iwerks did most of the animation and helped design Mickey.

statement: One of the Seven Dwarfs is named Sniffy.
why: It's Sneezy. The seven are Doc, Grumpy, Happy, Sleepy, Bashful, Sneezy and Dopey.

statement: In The Lion King, Scar is Simba's grandfather.
why: Scar is Simba's uncle, Mufasa's younger brother.

statement: Woody's horse in Toy Story is named Buttercup.
why: Woody's horse is Bullseye. Buttercup is the unicorn from Toy Story 3.

statement: Buzz Lightyear's catchphrase is "To the stars and beyond!"
why: It's "To infinity and beyond!"

statement: Nemo's dad in Finding Nemo is named Gill.
why: His dad is Marlin. Gill is the leader of the fish tank gang.

statement: Gaston gives Belle her huge library in Beauty and the Beast.
why: The Beast gives her the library. Gaston thinks reading is a waste of time.

statement: Princess Jasmine's pet tiger is named Abu.
why: Her tiger is Rajah. Abu is Aladdin's monkey.

statement: Pinocchio's nose grows when he gets scared.
why: It grows when he tells a lie.

statement: Peter Pan's fairy friend is named Silvermist.
why: It's Tinker Bell. Silvermist is one of her fairy friends from the later Disney Fairies films.

statement: Lightning McQueen's racing number is 99.
why: Lightning McQueen is number 95.

statement: Kristoff's reindeer in Frozen is named Rudolph.
why: His reindeer is Sven.

statement: Will Smith voiced Mushu in the original Mulan.
why: Eddie Murphy voiced Mushu in 1998.

statement: "Hakuna Matata" means "live forever".
why: It's Swahili for "no worries".

statement: The original Disneyland is in Florida.
why: Disneyland is in Anaheim, California. Florida has Walt Disney World.

statement: Tinker Bell has spoken lines in the original 1953 Peter Pan.
why: She never speaks in the film. She talks through bell sounds and expressions.

statement: Cinderella's fairy godmother turns a watermelon into her carriage.
why: It's a pumpkin.

statement: Elsa builds her ice palace while singing "Into the Unknown".
why: She builds it during Let It Go. Into the Unknown is from Frozen II.

statement: The Lion King is based on Romeo and Juliet.
why: It's loosely inspired by Shakespeare's Hamlet: a murdered king, a scheming uncle and a prince who must return.

statement: Snow White falls asleep after eating a poisoned pear.
why: It's a poisoned apple.

statement: In Monsters, Inc., the city runs on children's laughter from the very start.
why: It runs on screams at first. The switch to laughter only happens at the end.

statement: Baymax comes from the movie Wreck-It Ralph.
why: Baymax is from Big Hero 6.

statement: In Up, Carl's late wife is named Edith.
why: Her name is Ellie.

statement: Phil, Hercules' trainer, is a centaur.
why: Phil is a satyr: half man, half goat.

statement: Cinderella was the first Disney princess.
why: Snow White came first in 1937. Cinderella followed in 1950.

statement: Ratatouille is set in London.
why: Remy cooks in Paris.

statement: King Triton rules the underwater kingdom of Atlantis.
why: His kingdom is Atlantica. Atlantis is a different Disney movie.

statement: Lilo & Stitch is set in California.
why: It's set on the Hawaiian island of Kauaʻi.
